title: Priority and reader lifetime have separate responsibilities
takeaway: Joining changes retained work scope. The scheduler observes that change only through a retained scope reference at a later drain.
assumptions: This is a schematic responsibility map of current code. The dashed connection is conditional: the supplied source does not show a scheduler caller passing the work scope.

entities.label: Caller scope
entities.summary: Provides effective priority through AsyncLocalStorage and parent scopes.

entities.label: Shared GitHub read
entities.summary: Creates shared GitHub work and joins it before registering each reader.

entities.label: GitHubWork
entities.summary: Retains the operation promise and mutable priority scope across awaits.

entities.label: Shared read
entities.summary: Owns reader accounting and the shared abort controller.

entities.label: Scheduler
entities.summary: Selects pending work by effective priority and applies execution admission conditions.

relationships.label: Read under caller context
relationships.summary: The wrapper joins work under the current caller priority.

relationships.label: Join existing work
relationships.summary: A higher-priority join mutates the retained work scope.

relationships.label: Register reader
relationships.summary: After joining work, the wrapper requests a reader promise with the caller's cancellation signal.

relationships.label: Conditional scope handoff
relationships.summary: The scheduler retains a supplied scope object; no supplied caller establishes this handoff from GitHubWork.

plan.question: How can an interactive caller promote existing work without restarting it or interrupting active tasks?
plan.visualApproach: Place the shared GitHub wrapper between caller context and retained work scope. Put reader lifetime below the wrapper and scheduler admission beside the scope. Use a dashed connection for the unshown scope handoff.
plan.whyThisForm: The connected map separates priority ownership from reader cancellation and makes the missing caller connection explicit.
plan.encodings: Solid arrows show calls established by the source. The dashed arrow shows a conditional scope handoff. Separate scheduler regions distinguish pending selection from active execution. Every participant is context.
plan.motion: Use a static map. The important relationship is shared scope identity, not movement; animation would imply an enqueue sequence that the supplied callers do not establish.
plan.prediction: A pending task given only a priority string will not observe a later mutation of the work scope.
plan.restingState: The scope mutation, conditional scheduler connection, admission conditions, and separate reader lifetime remain visible.

scenarios.title: Existing work receives a higher-priority caller
scenarios.input: An interactive caller reads an existing shared GitHub operation.

frames.title: Retained scope connects promotion to selection
frames.caption: The join changes scope, not the active operation. Pending selection can use that change when the scheduler retains the scope.
